steps.title: Import Vue and ref from 'vue'
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the vue module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and available for use in the component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref, which are essential for building reactive components in Vue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Accordion component
steps.instruction: Define a Vue component named 'Accordion' with a script section that exports a default object and a template section that returns a div.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component is defined by exporting a default object inside a script tag. The template tag contains the HTML structure.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a basic Vue component structure
steps.seedCode:
<script>
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Define the Accordion component here
</script>
<template>
  <!-- Add template content here -->
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have a complete Vue component structure with script and template sections ready for the accordion implementation.
successCriteria: The Accordion component is defined with a script section that exports a default object and a template section containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully created the basic Vue component structure for the accordion.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the script section with export default and the template section with a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't complete. Remember to define the Accordion component with both script and template sections.

steps.hint: Use the ref function to create a reactive reference containing your array of accordion items.

successCriteria: The 'items' ref is defined with an array containing at least one object that has both 'title' and 'content' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the accordion items data structure. This will serve as the foundation for your accordion content.

steps.feedbackWrong: The items data wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use ref() to create a reactive reference containing an array of objects with title and content properties.

steps.title: Initialize active item state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive variable called 'activeItem' using ref() and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Use the ref() function you imported earlier to create reactive state. The syntax is: const variableName = ref(initialValue).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a reactive variable
const count = ref(0)

steps.title: Define toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named toggleItem that takes an index parameter and toggles the activeItem ref between that index and null.
steps.hint: The toggleItem function should check if activeItem.value equals the clicked index. If it does, set activeItem.value to null; otherwise, set it to the clicked index.
steps.seedCode:
<script>
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Define the Accordion component here

      { title: 'Section 2', content: 'Content for section 2' },
      { title: 'Section 3', content: 'Content for section 3' }
    ])
    
    // Create a reactive variable for tracking the active accordion item
    const activeItem = ref(null)
    
    // Define toggleItem function here
    
    return {}
  }
}
</script>
<template>
  <!-- Add template content here -->
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggleItem function is defined and will be used to handle opening and closing accordion items.
successCriteria: A toggleItem function is defined that toggles activeItem.value between the clicked index and null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the toggle handler function. This function will control which accordion item is open.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the toggleItem function needs to properly toggle activeItem.value. Check if it correctly sets the value to null when the same item is clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleItem function is missing or doesn't toggle activeItem.value correctly. It should check if activeItem.value equals the clicked index and set it to null if true, otherwise set it to the clicked index.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In the template section, add a div element with the class 'accordion' to serve as the main container for your accordion component.
steps.hint: The template section should contain a single root element. Start by adding a div with the class attribute set to 'accordion'.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a main container div in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a root div element with class 'accordion' that will contain all accordion items.
successCriteria: A div element with class='accordion' is present in the template section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the main container for your accordion. This provides the structure needed to hold the individual accordion items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element with exactly class='accordion' in the template section.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template section should contain a div element with class='accordion' as the main container. Check that you've added this element correctly.

steps.title: Add v-for loop for accordion items
steps.instruction: Inside the accordion container div, add a new div element that uses the v-for directive to loop through the items array. Use 'item' as the alias and 'index' as the key.
steps.hint: Remember that v-for syntax in Vue is v-for="(item, index) in items". You'll need to add this directive to a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a div element with v-for directive that iterates through the items array, preparing to render each accordion item.
successCriteria: A div element with v-for="(item, index) in items" directive is added inside the accordion container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the v-for loop to iterate through accordion items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using the correct v-for syntax with both item and index parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The v-for loop wasn't added correctly. Make sure you're using v-for="(item, index) in items" on a div element inside the accordion container.

steps.title: Add accordion header with click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the v-for loop in your template, add a button element for each accordion item header. Bind its click event to the toggleItem function, passing the current item's index as an argument.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to call toggleItem with the index parameter from your v-for loop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a click handler to a button in Vue
<button @click="handleClick(index)">{{ item.title }}</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each accordion item will have a clickable header button that will trigger the toggle functionality when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element is added inside the v-for loop with @click binding to toggleItem, passing the item index as argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added clickable headers to your accordion items. Each button will now trigger the toggle functionality when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the button element with the @click directive and passed the index as an argument to toggleItem.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button with click handler wasn't added correctly. Remember to add a button element inside the v-for loop with @click="toggleItem(index)".

steps.title: Add conditional content display
steps.instruction: Inside your v-for loop, add a div element after the header that uses v-show to conditionally display the content of the current accordion item when it's active.
steps.hint: Use v-show with a condition that checks if the current item's index matches the activeItem value. The div should contain the item's content property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional display with v-show
Content appears when isVisible is true
steps.expectedOutcome: Each accordion item will have a content area that shows only when that item is active, using Vue's v-show directive.
successCriteria: A div element with v-show directive is added inside the v-for loop that conditionally displays the item's content based on whether the current index equals activeItem.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional content display using v-show. The accordion content will now appear only when its corresponding header is active.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a div element with v-show that checks if the current item index matches activeItem, and displays the item's content inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional content display isn't quite right. You need to add a div element with v-show inside the v-for loop that shows the item's content when that item is active.

steps.title: Add styling classes and final polish
steps.instruction: Add CSS classes to the header and content elements for visual styling. Use 'accordion-header' for the header and 'accordion-content' for the content div.
steps.hint: Add class attributes to the existing HTML elements to apply styling.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding CSS classes to elements
Content here
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion headers and content areas will have CSS classes applied for styling.
successCriteria: The header div has class="accordion-header" and the content div has class="accordion-content".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the CSS classes needed for styling the accordion.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some classes, but make sure both the header and content divs have the correct class names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS classes were not added correctly. Check that you added class="accordion-header" to the header div and class="accordion-content" to the content div.
